questions.q: In the communication process, the conversion of an idea or message into words, signs or symbols by the sender is called...
questions.explanation: Encoding is the sender’s act of putting the message into a form that can be transmitted. Decoding is done by the receiver, feedback is the receiver’s response, and the medium is the channel through which the message travels.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha wants to move 300 bags of rice to a customer in Nnewi, about 30 kilometres away, with direct delivery to the customer’s store. Which mode of transport is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Road transport is the most suitable because it provides flexible door-to-door delivery over a short distance. Rail and water transport usually require terminals and additional handling, while pipelines are used for fluids or gases, not bagged rice.

questions.q: An insurance company may reject a claim on goods insured by a trader who has no financial interest in the goods. This is because the trader lacks...
questions.explanation: Insurable interest means that the insured must stand to suffer financial loss if the insured property is damaged or destroyed. Without such a financial relationship, the trader cannot make a valid claim. Subrogation and contribution are principles used when handling claims involving other parties or more than one insurer, not proof of the trader's own financial interest.

questions.q: A newly incorporated company in Enugu wants to state the rules for appointing directors and conducting general meetings. These internal rules are contained in the...
questions.explanation: The Articles of Association regulate the internal management of a company, including meetings and appointment of directors. The Memorandum of Association deals mainly with the company’s external relations and objects, the certificate proves incorporation, and a prospectus invites the public to subscribe for shares.

questions.q: A flour milling company buys a bakery that uses its flour to produce bread. This is an example of...
questions.explanation: Vertical integration occurs when firms at different stages of production or distribution join together, as when a flour mill acquires a bakery that uses its flour. Horizontal integration involves firms at the same stage, while a conglomerate merger joins unrelated businesses.

questions.q: The marketing mix consists of product, price, promotion and...
questions.explanation: The main elements of the marketing mix are product, price, place and promotion. Place covers distribution and making the product available to buyers, while packaging is part of product, publicity is part of promotion, and profit is a business result rather than a marketing mix element.

questions.q: A beverage company sells a new drink in two selected towns for three months before launching it nationwide in order to assess customer response. This activity is called...
questions.explanation: Test marketing involves introducing a product in a limited area on a trial basis to find out how customers respond before a full launch. Market segmentation divides buyers into groups, product differentiation makes a product stand out from rivals, and sales promotion consists of short-term incentives to boost sales.

questions.q: A firm in Lagos wants to sell a used delivery van. It places a short notice under 'For Sale' in a newspaper, giving only the van’s details and a phone number. This is an example of...
questions.explanation: Classified advertising consists of short paid notices grouped under headings such as 'For Sale', usually with limited design. Display advertising uses larger designed spaces, public relations builds goodwill rather than directly selling an item, and personal selling involves direct oral persuasion by a salesperson.

questions.q: Ngozi places ₦150,000 in a fixed deposit account at 8% simple interest per annum for 6 months. How much interest will she earn at the end of the period?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is calculated as principal × rate × time, so ₦150,000 × 8/100 × 6/12 = ₦6,000. The figure ₦12,000 is the interest for a full year rather than for six months.

questions.q: A cheque presented for payment by a customer in Abeokuta is returned unpaid because the drawer's account has insufficient funds. Such a cheque is best described as
questions.explanation: A cheque is dishonoured when the bank refuses to pay it, for example because there are insufficient funds in the drawer's account. A stale cheque is one presented after the permitted period, while a crossed cheque must be paid through a bank account.

questions.q: Tolu bought 400 shares of a quoted company at ₦25 per share. The company later paid a dividend of ₦1.50 per share. What is the dividend yield on Tolu's investment?
questions.explanation: Dividend yield is dividend per share divided by cost per share, multiplied by 100: ₦1.50 ÷ ₦25 × 100 = 6%. Using the total dividend of ₦600 on the total cost of ₦10,000 gives the same result.

questions.q: On the Nigerian Exchange, the person or firm that keeps a company's register of shareholders and records changes in share ownership is the
questions.explanation: The registrar maintains the register of shareholders and records transfers and changes in ownership. A stockbroker buys and sells shares for clients, while an issuing house assists with new issues and an underwriter guarantees subscription to an issue.

questions.q: The index that is widely used on the Nigerian Exchange to measure the general movement of prices of quoted shares is the
questions.explanation: The All-Share Index tracks the general movement of share prices on the Nigerian Exchange. The Consumer Price Index measures changes in consumer prices, while the Monetary Policy Rate and Treasury Bill Rate are monetary and short-term interest rate indicators.

questions.q: Many small firms that make shoes are concentrated in Aba because they share skilled labour, suppliers and infrastructure. This concentration of firms in one area is best described as
questions.explanation: Localization of industry occurs when related firms concentrate in a particular area due to shared facilities, labour and suppliers. Delocalization is the opposite, involving the dispersal of industries to different areas.

questions.q: Musa resigns from paid employment to start a block-making business. He provides the capital, organises labour and bears the risk of loss. The reward Musa expects for performing this function is
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur organises the other factors of production and bears risk, and the reward for this function is profit. Wages reward labour, rent rewards land, and interest rewards capital.

questions.q: Chinedu receives an email that looks like it comes from his bank. It asks him to click a link and enter his card details to 'reactivate' his account. This fraudulent practice is best described as
questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages that imitate a trusted organisation to trick people into revealing financial or personal information. Spamming is the sending of unsolicited messages, while hacking involves gaining unauthorised access to a computer system.

questions.q: Aminat in Maiduguri is considering buying a phone from an online store. Which of the following is a major disadvantage of buying the phone online rather than from a physical shop?
options: She will have a narrower range of phones to choose from
She may not be able to examine the phone before paying for it
She can place orders only during the shop's working hours
She cannot compare prices from different sellers
questions.explanation: A key disadvantage of online buying is that the buyer may not physically inspect the goods before payment, creating a risk of receiving a damaged or different item. Online stores generally offer a wider range of goods, allow orders at any time, and make price comparison easier.

questions.q: Chief Okafor in Lagos imports bicycle parts from India and later re-exports them to a buyer in Ghana without changing their form. The trade involved is best described as
questions.explanation: Entrepot trade occurs when imported goods are later re-exported, usually without processing. Bilateral trade refers to trade between two countries under an agreement, while invisible trade involves services rather than goods.

questions.q: A Lagos importer must pay a supplier in China 8,000 US dollars. If the exchange rate is ₦1,550 to 1 US dollar, how much naira will the importer need, excluding bank charges?
questions.explanation: The naira required is 8,000 × ₦1,550 = ₦12,400,000. The other amounts arise from shifting the decimal place or using the wrong number of zeros.

questions.q: A Nigerian seller agrees to place goods on board a ship at Apapa, after which the buyer bears the freight and insurance costs. The trade term used is
questions.explanation: Under Free on Board, the seller's duty ends when the goods are placed on board the vessel at the named port of shipment. Cost, Insurance and Freight would require the seller to pay freight and insurance to the destination, while Ex-Works places the goods at the seller's premises.

questions.q: In consumer protection, the principle of caveat emptor means that
options: the government must fix prices of essential goods
the manufacturer is always liable for any injury caused by a product
the buyer should examine goods carefully before buying them
the seller must replace all faulty goods free of charge
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor means 'let the buyer beware', placing a duty on the buyer to inspect goods and make prudent choices before purchase. It is not a rule that sellers must automatically replace faulty goods or that manufacturers are always liable.

questions.q: A large retail outlet in Aba displays only samples of goods, requires customers to pay cash at the counter and then collect their purchases from a warehouse section. This outlet is best described as a
questions.explanation: A cash-and-carry sells mainly for cash and keeps goods in bulk in a warehouse area, with limited display for customers. A department store has separate departments offering varied goods and services, while a consumer co-operative is owned by its members.

questions.q: A manufacturer sends a retailer a document informing him that the goods ordered have been dispatched. This document is an
questions.explanation: An advice note informs the buyer that the ordered goods have been sent, helping the buyer prepare to receive them. An invoice claims payment, a debit note records an amount owed by the buyer, and a bill of lading is a shipping document used in carriage of goods by sea.

questions.q: A road transport company in Onitsha receives goods from a trader for delivery to Kano. Which document should the company issue to acknowledge that it has taken charge of the goods for carriage?
questions.explanation: A waybill, also called a consignment note, is issued by a road carrier to acknowledge receipt of goods for carriage and show the terms of delivery. A bill of lading is used mainly in sea transport, while a manifest lists cargo on a ship or aircraft and a certificate of origin shows where goods were produced.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Kano wants to inform his regular retailers in different towns about new credit terms and ensure that each retailer receives a written copy addressed personally. Which means of communication is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A circular letter is a written message sent to many people, with each copy addressed to the recipient, and it can be kept for future reference. A telephone call is oral, while a newspaper advertisement or radio announcement is a public message not individually addressed to each retailer.

questions.q: A cement factory in Ogun State needs to move very large quantities of limestone over a long inland distance at the lowest possible cost, and speed is not important. Which mode of transport is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Rail transport is best suited to bulky, low-value goods over long inland distances because it carries large loads at relatively low cost per tonne-kilometre. Air transport is too costly, pipelines are for liquids or gases, and road transport is less economical for very large long-distance loads.

questions.q: A lorry belonging to Musa damaged the shop of Ngozi in Kaduna. Ngozi's insurer paid for the repairs and later sued Musa to recover the amount paid. Which insurance principle allows the insurer to do this?
questions.explanation: Subrogation gives an insurer that has indemnified a policyholder the right to take over the policyholder's legal claim against the party responsible for the loss. Contribution applies when two or more policies cover the same risk, insurable interest concerns the financial relationship to the subject matter, and proximate cause is the effective cause of a loss.

questions.q: A trader in Ibadan is sending goods by lorry to Kano and wants cover against loss or damage to the goods while they are on the road. Which type of insurance is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Goods-in-transit insurance covers goods while they are being carried from one place to another by land. Motor insurance covers the vehicle and third-party liabilities, marine insurance covers sea carriage, and fidelity guarantee insurance covers losses from dishonest employees.

questions.q: A woman in Aba fills an insurance proposal form but hides the fact that her shop is next to a fuel station. The insurer later discovers this. Which principle has she violated?
questions.explanation: Insurance contracts require utmost good faith, which means the proposer must disclose all material facts that could affect the insurer's decision. Indemnity concerns restoring the insured to the pre-loss financial position, contribution concerns sharing a loss among insurers, and subrogation allows an insurer to recover from a responsible third party.

questions.q: In a company limited by shares, the liability of a shareholder who has not fully paid for his shares is limited to
options: all debts owed by the company
the amount unpaid on the shares
the value of his personal property
questions.explanation: A shareholder in a company limited by shares is liable only for any amount still unpaid on the nominal value of the shares held. The company is a separate legal person and its creditors cannot generally claim the shareholder's personal property beyond that unpaid amount, while turnover measures sales and not liability.

questions.q: A cosmetics company in Lagos produces different creams for teenagers, nursing mothers and elderly women after studying the needs of each group. This division of the market into buyers with similar needs is called
questions.explanation: Market segmentation is the process of dividing a broad market into smaller groups of buyers with similar needs or characteristics so that products and marketing can be better matched to each group. Market research is the gathering of information, personal selling is direct persuasion by a seller, and packaging protects or presents a product.

questions.q: Which statement best describes advertising as a promotional activity?
options: It is the process of setting prices for goods in a supermarket.
It is a face-to-face discussion between a seller and a buyer.
It is a free public notice that must be broadcast by all media houses.
It is a paid, non-personal message from an identified sponsor about a product or organisation.
questions.explanation: Advertising is paid for by an identified sponsor and reaches many people through media without personal contact between seller and buyer. Face-to-face persuasion is personal selling, while price setting is a pricing decision and advertising is not required to be free.

questions.q: The central bank function of providing financial assistance to a bank that is temporarily unable to meet its obligations is known as
questions.explanation: A central bank acts as lender of last resort when it gives emergency financial support to a bank facing temporary liquidity problems. Open market operation involves buying or selling securities, moral suasion is persuasion, and deposit insurance is handled by a separate deposit insurance body.

questions.q: A Lagos importer wants his bank to assure a foreign supplier that payment will be made when the shipping documents are presented. The bank should issue a
questions.explanation: A letter of credit is a bank's promise to pay a supplier once the required shipping documents are presented, which gives the foreign supplier assurance of payment. A standing order is only a regular payment instruction, while an overdraft is a borrowing facility and a treasury bill is a short-term government security.

questions.q: Mariam deposits ₦180,000 in a savings account that pays simple interest at 8% per annum. What interest will she earn in 15 months?
questions.explanation: Using simple interest, I = P × R × T = ₦180,000 × 8/100 × 15/12 = ₦18,000. The value ₦14,400 would be earned for only one year, while ₦21,600 would apply if the period were 18 months.

questions.q: A shareholder in a quoted company owns 20,000 ordinary shares. If the company declares a dividend of 30 kobo per share, how much will the shareholder receive?
questions.explanation: A dividend of 30 kobo per share is ₦0.30 per share, so the total is 20,000 × ₦0.30 = ₦6,000. The smaller figure ₦600 would result from using 3 kobo per share instead of 30 kobo.

questions.q: Before a public company sells its shares to the public, it issues a document containing details of the company and the share offer. This document is called a
questions.explanation: A prospectus gives investors the information they need to decide whether to buy the shares being offered to the public. A share certificate is issued after shares are bought, a dividend warrant pays dividends, and a debenture trust deed relates to borrowing rather than a share offer.

questions.q: The reward paid to capital as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: Capital earns interest, while land earns rent, labour earns wages or salaries, and entrepreneurship earns profit. Interest is therefore the correct reward for the use of capital in production.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan sells a used textbook to another student through an online marketplace. This type of e-commerce transaction is best described as
questions.explanation: In this transaction both the seller and the buyer are individual consumers, so it is consumer-to-consumer e-commerce. Business-to-business and business-to-consumer transactions involve a business as one of the main parties.

questions.q: When an online shopper in Abuja enters her card details, her bank sends a one-time code to her phone which she must enter to complete the payment. This measure is mainly intended to
options: reduce the risk of unauthorised use of the card
guarantee the quality of the goods
remove the need for a bank account
speed up delivery of the goods
questions.explanation: A one-time code helps authenticate the person making the payment and reduces the risk that someone else is using the card fraudulently. It does not affect delivery speed, guarantee product quality, or replace the need for a bank account.

questions.q: In a foreign trade contract quoted as c.i.f., the seller is responsible for
options: the cost of the goods only, while the buyer arranges insurance and freight
the cost of insurance only, while the buyer pays for the goods and freight
the cost of freight only, while the buyer pays for the goods and insurance
the cost of the goods, insurance and freight up to the named destination port
questions.explanation: C.i.f. stands for cost, insurance and freight; the quoted price includes all three up to the agreed destination. The other arrangements divide these charges between buyer and seller and therefore describe different terms.

questions.q: The Nigerian government allows only importers with special permits to bring a particular type of textile into the country. This method of controlling foreign trade is called
questions.explanation: Import licensing restricts imports by requiring importers to obtain permission before bringing in specified goods. An export subsidy assists exporters, a customs drawback refunds duty, and devaluation changes the exchange rate rather than issuing import permits.

questions.q: A customer in Kaduna is told by the only gas dealer in her area that she must buy a particular brand of cylinder because no other brand will be accepted in the estate. Which consumer right is most directly denied?
questions.explanation: The right to choose allows consumers to select from competing goods and brands without being forced to accept one brand. Being protected from harm, receiving adequate product information, and obtaining compensation for defective goods concern other consumer rights.

questions.q: A trader in Ibadan advertises a pressing iron at ₦15,000, but when a customer arrives he says the price is for the stand only and the iron itself costs ₦25,000. This practice is an example of
questions.explanation: The advertisement attracts the customer with a false price and then changes the terms, which is deceptive advertising. It is not an after-sales service, a credit sale arrangement, or legal responsibility for defective goods.

questions.q: A trader in Aba refuses to replace a cloth that shrank after washing, saying that the buyer should have examined the material before paying. The principle underlying the trader's stand is
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor means let the buyer beware, implying that the buyer should examine goods before purchase. Consumer protection laws now limit this principle, but the trader's statement is the classic caveat emptor position.

questions.q: A large retail store in Abuja is divided into sections for groceries, furniture, clothing and electronics, all under one roof and owned by one firm. This retail organisation is a
questions.explanation: A department store is a single large retail shop divided into sections, each handling a separate line of goods under one roof. A chain store has several branches, a supermarket mainly sells food and household items, and a consumer co-operative is owned by members.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Onitsha collects information from retailers about changes in demand and passes it to a manufacturer in Aba, while also holding the manufacturer's stock in his warehouse. These services are rendered by the wholesaler to the
questions.explanation: By informing the manufacturer about demand and holding the manufacturer's stock, the wholesaler helps production planning and reduces the manufacturer's storage burden. These particular services are not rendered directly to final consumers, retailers or a commercial bank.

questions.q: A document prepared by an exporter and certified by the consul of the importing country, showing the value, quantity and description of goods for customs purposes, is called a
questions.explanation: A consular invoice is certified by the importing country's consul and helps customs assess the goods. A pro forma invoice is a quotation or advance invoice, a credit note corrects an overcharge, and a statement of account summarizes transactions over a period.

questions.q: The use of a house journal by a firm is mainly to
options: serve as a legal contract between the firm and its customers
record the minutes of board meetings
advertise the firm's products to the general public
provide employees with information about the firm and promote a sense of belonging
questions.explanation: A house journal is an internal communication medium for staff, used to share company news, policies and achievements. It is not a public advertising medium, minutes record formal proceedings, and it has no contractual force with customers.

questions.q: Chief Eze operates a shopping mall in Enugu. He takes an insurance policy to meet claims from customers who slip and injure themselves in the mall. The policy is
questions.explanation: Public liability insurance covers a business against claims from third parties, such as customers injured on the premises or whose property is damaged. Employer's liability covers employees, fidelity guarantee covers dishonesty by employees, and burglary insurance covers theft by breaking in.

questions.q: A trader in Kano insured her stock for ₦900,000 although the actual value of the stock at the time of a fire was ₦1,200,000. The fire destroyed stock valued at ₦360,000. If the policy contains an average clause, how much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Under the average clause, the insurer pays (sum insured ÷ actual value at the time of loss) × loss. Here, (₦900,000 ÷ ₦1,200,000) × ₦360,000 = 0.75 × ₦360,000 = ₦270,000. Paying ₦360,000 ignores under-insurance, while ₦480,000 wrongly reverses the ratio.

questions.q: A bakery in Ibadan insures its building and machinery against fire. It also buys a policy that will pay for the profit it loses and the extra cost of renting another bakery while repairs are done after a fire. This policy is
questions.explanation: Consequential loss insurance covers loss of profit and additional expenses arising from interruption of business after an insured event such as fire. Fidelity guarantee covers dishonest employees, public liability covers injury or damage to third parties, and marine insurance covers sea transport risks.

questions.q: A new sachet water company in Abeokuta sets a low price for its product in order to attract many buyers quickly and gain a large share of the market. This pricing strategy is called
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing uses a low introductory price to encourage buyers to try a new product and build market share quickly. Price skimming starts with a high price, psychological pricing appeals to buyer perception, and cost-plus pricing adds a markup to production cost.

questions.q: A salesperson from a paint company in Lagos visits hardware retailers, explains the qualities of a new emulsion paint and persuades them to place orders. This promotional activity is
questions.explanation: Personal selling involves face-to-face persuasive communication between a salesperson and prospective buyers. Advertising is paid non-personal promotion through mass media, publicity is unpaid media attention, and sales promotion uses short-term incentives such as discounts or free samples.

questions.q: A trader in Kano writes ₦75,000 as the price of a bag of rice in his records before any customer buys it. This use of money illustrates its function as a
questions.explanation: Money serves as a unit of account when it is used to measure and quote the value of goods and services. No payment has yet been made, so it is not acting as a medium of exchange. Keeping money for future use is the store of value function, while deferred payment relates to settling credit later.

questions.q: Which of the following is a liability of a commercial bank in Nigeria?
options: Treasury bills held by the bank
questions.explanation: Customers' deposits are liabilities because the bank owes that money to depositors and must repay it on demand or as agreed. Loans and advances, treasury bills and bank buildings are assets of the bank since they are resources owned by the bank or money owed to it.

questions.q: Which of the following securities gives the holder the right to receive interest and be repaid the principal, but not to vote at a company's general meeting?
questions.explanation: A debenture is a loan to a company, so the holder receives interest and repayment of principal as a creditor. It does not carry voting rights at shareholders' meetings. Ordinary shares carry ownership and voting rights, preference shares are shares with priority dividends, and a share warrant gives a right to acquire shares.

questions.q: An investor on the Nigerian Exchange sells shares he does not own, hoping to buy them back later at a lower price and make a profit. Such an investor is called a
questions.explanation: A bear expects share prices to fall and therefore sells now in the hope of buying back later at a lower price. A bull expects prices to rise, while a stag applies for new shares mainly to resell them quickly at a premium. A jobber is a dealer who trades in shares on his own account.

questions.q: In a small garment factory, one worker cuts the cloth, another sews the garments, and a third fixes the buttons. This arrangement is an example of
questions.explanation: Division of labour occurs when a production process is split into different tasks performed by different workers. Labour mobility refers to the movement of workers between jobs or places, mass production is large-scale production of standardized goods, and localization of industry is the clustering of similar firms in an area.

questions.q: A delivery company in Jos uses a van for six years to distribute goods to customers. In production, the van is an example of
questions.explanation: Fixed capital consists of durable assets used repeatedly in production over a long period, such as a delivery van. Working capital is used up in the production process, land refers to natural resources, and a consumer good is meant for final consumption rather than business use.
